youtube.baslik: Can a sound the person says they cannot hear trigger a reflex? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: The acoustic reflex appears when a sound is well above the hearing threshold; in people with normal hearing, reflex thresholds are usually between 70 and 100 dB HL. In the example case, with the stimulus in the left ear, reflexes are present at 70 dB HL at 500 and 1000 Hz, the same level at which the person says they do not hear the sound. If the reflex is present at a level equal to or better than the claimed threshold, the claimed threshold cannot be real; but an absent reflex is not proof on its own.
